title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
prompt:
Given bar heights of a histogram (each of width 1), return the area of the largest rectangle that fits inside.

**Example**: `[2,1,5,6,2,3]` → `10` (the `5,6` bars give 5×2).

A monotonic (increasing) stack of `{startIndex, height}`: when a shorter bar appears, pop taller bars and settle their rectangles — each popped bar could extend left to where it was first pushed.
hints: Stack holds `{start, height}` with heights increasing bottom→top.
When bar i is shorter than the top, pop it: its rectangle spans from its recorded start to i, so area = height × (i - start). Remember the leftmost popped start — bar i can extend back that far.
After the loop, settle whatever remains: each extends to the end of the histogram.

solution.explanation: O(n): each bar is pushed and popped once. A bar's maximal rectangle is bounded on the right by the first shorter bar (which triggers its pop) and on the left by where it was pushed (inherited when it absorbed taller bars in front of it). Bars never popped run to the far right edge.
